findings.title: JWT signing secret is hard-coded in source.
Search term is interpolated into SQL, allowing SQL injection.
bcrypt.compare is not awaited, so the always-truthy Promise lets any password log in.
Internal error message and stack trace are returned to the client.
findings.evidence: return reply.code(500).send({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack });

findings.title: JWT verification does not pin the accepted algorithms.
Synchronous bcrypt hashing blocks the event loop on every sign-up.
Unknown emails return before any bcrypt work, enabling account enumeration by timing.
DATABASE_URL is used without checking it is set, so misconfiguration fails late.
findings.evidence: const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });

findings.title: No security headers (helmet) and no log redaction of the authorization header.
console.log bypasses the structured request logger.
Loose equality used instead of strict equality.
Commented-out code left in the change.
findings.evidence: // const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '7d' });

findings.title: No SIGINT/SIGTERM handler to close the server and pool gracefully.
Admin usage route is registered before the auth and admin-role middleware, so it is publicly reachable.
Any authenticated user can delete any document; no ownership check (IDOR).
findings.evidence: const { rowCount } = await pool.query('DELETE FROM documents WHERE id = $1', [req.params.id]);

findings.title: Concurrent `+= await` reads the subtotal before awaiting, so meter charges overwrite each other (lost update).
findings.evidence: subtotalCents += await meterChargeCents(teamId, meter, start, end);

findings.title: Amount due is computed and stored as floating-point dollars, risking rounding errors in money.
sendMail promise is returned without await, so SMTP failures escape the try/catch.
Pooled client is released only on success; any error (including the timeout) leaks the connection with statement_timeout still set.
Adding a month with setUTCMonth overflows on the 29th-31st (e.g. Jan 31 becomes Mar 3).
SMTP on port 587 does not require TLS, so credentials can be sent in clear if STARTTLS is stripped.
